title: Crestfall Fulfillment — integration raw notes
body:
Context:
- Customer: Crestfall Fulfillment (third-party logistics). Large regional warehouses in US East + Midwest. Sensitive PII in shipment manifests, regulated customer SLAs.
- Goal: prototype an LLM assistant for exception triage (incoming pick/pack errors, address corrections, carrier communications) that can run inside their VPC / air-gapped colo.
- Meeting: intake call 2024-11-12, follow-up architecture session 2024-11-29. Notes below are rough capture from both calls + internal thinking.

Attendees (customer + Redwood):
- Crestfall: Priya Nair (Head of Ops), Jonah Reeves (SRE), Mila Torres (Integration PM)
- Redwood: Asha Patel (CS lead), Marcus Li (SE - private deployments), Rina Gomez (Security eng)

High-level ask / acceptance criteria (customer language):
- Run a small assistant that processes pick/pack exception tickets and suggests next steps to ops staff.
- Latency needs: suggestions in <300ms p95 for interactive triage (agent UI for humans).
- Throughput: steady 80–120 req/s during peak shift windows; spikes to 320 req/s occasionally.
- Data residency: logs & model inputs cannot leave their VPC; metadata (non-PII) telemetry ok to send to Redwood if agreed.
- SLA: 99.5% service availability for the pilot window (2 months) and rollback to degraded local-only mode on failure.

Environment constraints / infra notes from Jonah:
- On-prem rack at colo: 4 x NVIDIA A10 (shared with other workloads). KVM-based virtualization; uses internal private network with NAT egress blocked.
- They have an HSM for key storage (YubiHSM variant) and use Vault for secrets.
- Internal CI/CD runs in an air-gapped cluster; any Redwood artifacts must be signed and staged.
- Ops team uses Datadog internally; logs need to be routed to internal NGFW.

Initial suggested Redwood deployment model (SE recommendation):
- Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) with a local inference plane inside their VPC.
- Dedicated pool: reserve 2 GPUs for the pilot model (quantized variant) and allow burst to 4 GPUs for >1min spikes via autoscale policy set to "warden-burst".
- Kernel/quantization profile: int8 with PF32 fallback for heavy sequences. Model candidate: Llama2-13B quantized -> test Mistral 7B as lower-cost fallback for ultra-low-latency short prompts.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix caching for common instruction templates (address normalization).

Technical requirements gathered:
- Model persistence: must be stored on encrypted local NVMe and mounted into runtime; checksum verification on boot.
- Key integration: Redwood runtime should call their Vault via mTLS using a service cert; HSM-signing for decryption ops.
- No outbound internet during execution; control plane can be operated via bastion with explicit allowlist.
- Observability: token-level latency, per-request model version, and 95/99 percentiles sent to internal Datadog; sensitive prompt redaction before telemetry export.
- Audit logs: immutable append-only logs stored in S3-compatible object storage behind their firewall.

Gotchas / risk areas (callouts):
- Latency targets are aggressive given A10s with quantized 13B; must measure tail-latency under concurrent context + KV cache misses. Expect p95 ~350ms unless we adjust batching/sequence length.
- Network egress restrictions complicate remote support; need pre-approved signed diagnostic bundles and offline troubleshooting playbook.
- Ops wants deterministic behavior for escalations (same input -> same suggestion) for compliance. Using sampling or nucleus sampling in gen will break this. Need temperature=0.0 deterministic fallback for critical outputs.
- Tokenization mismatch: Crestfall uses legacy address templates with special unicode characters. Need to run a tokenization audit and include pre-tokenizer normalization in the pipeline.
- Embeddings vs. generation: They want similarity-based retrieval for prior exceptions but don't want embeddings leaving the VPC. Must ensure Redwood Private stores vectors locally or provide an on-prem embeddings-only service.

Open questions for customer / to clarify:
- Data retention policy: exact retention period for logs & redacted prompts? (Regulatory may require 7 years for shipment records).
- Acceptable telemetry: which fields are allowed to be exported to Redwood for billing/observability? (They suggested invoice-only hashes).
- Fallback policy: on failure, should we (a) run a local small-rule engine, (b) degrade to synchronous human queue, or (c) route to hosted Redwood with sanitized content? Need decision.
- Performance budget: are they willing to provision 8x A10 for pilot if we can't meet latency on 4x?

Proposed next steps (short term):
1) SE spike: Marcus to run a micro-benchmark (Llama2-13B int8) on a single A10 with their typical sequence distribution (avg 120 tokens, 95th 420). Deliverable: p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU mem footprint. Target by 2024-11-19.
2) Tokenization audit: Rina to prepare a small corpus (50 representative exception tickets) and run tokenizer diffs; report normalization rules needed. Target 2024-11-21.
3) Security onboarding checklist: generate signed artifact bundle and presigned offline installer for their air-gapped process. Asha to coordinate, due 2024-11-28.
4) Architecture diagram: produce runbook showing network flows, Vault integration, observability lanes, and failover modes. Draft by 2024-12-05.
5) Pilot acceptance criteria doc: collate SLA, latency targets, and rollback criteria. Joint doc with Crestfall (Mila lead).

Short-term owner tasks (who does what):
- Asha: coordinate artifact signing, send onboarding template, schedule demo for Priya week of 11/27.
- Marcus: run benchmarks, capture perf traces, test quantization profile.
- Rina: tokenization + security/secret flow validation.
- Priya (customer): provide sample dataset and confirm retention/telemetry policy.

Notes-to-self / helpful hints while prepping spike:
- Use Redwood "rapid-bench" harness with sequence length histogram support; instrument to simulate cache cold-starts.
- Try dynamic batching disabled first to get single-request latency baseline, then tune batch windows to see throughput/latency tradeoff.
- Push small model fallback (Mistral-7B) into canary route during pilot to reduce cost for short prompts.
- Precompute address-normalization regex + small post-processing verification to keep model prompt short (reduce tokens).

Conversation snippets (verbatim capture, informal):
- Priya: "If this thing takes forever, our floor won't use it — humans need the answer while they're on the pallet."
- Jonah: "We won't allow pinging the cloud unless we can read and agree to the hashes we send."
- Mila: "Let's try a 4-week pilot and adjust capacity after month 1 based on actual p95s."

Potential blockers for timeline:
- Legal sign-off on on-prem telemetry sharing — could add 2–3 weeks.
- HSM/Vault integration nuances (we may need a small shim if their HSM doesn't support our standard plugins).

If anything urgent: ping Marcus (se-marcus@redwood.ai) or Asha (asha@redwood.ai). I'll drop a lightweight checklist into the Confluence intake page and link the spike results when ready.

End of raw capture — rough, will clean up before sending to Crestfall for confirmation.
